niche.habitat: Basalt ridges, thermal vent fields, wind-scoured plates.
niche.diet: FeS₂, sulfur crystals, chemosynthetic biofilms, supercritical vent fluids.
niche.active: Thermally regulated; active above 150°C, stasis below 130°C.

body: Laminated silicate armor, lateral piezoelectric limbs, pincer claws, tucked ventral lattice-housing.

chains.trait: Broad, flattened carapace with sliding thermal joints.
links: Slides to reduce wind load and distribute shear stress
Dense atmosphere exerts high shear stress on low profile
3.2 bar pressure and abrasive silica dust scour open terrain

skill.effect: Carapace locks plates against wind and impact, reducing damage by 30% and passively venting excess heat.

chains.weakness: Slow to deploy; if struck before locking, thermal joints fracture and lose mobility.
observe: Plates ratchet open under pressure, sliding against each other
Dust piles on the dorsal curve but blows off the sides
Joints hiss as they slide to relieve thermal expansion

journal.en: A living slate that reads the wind like braille, armor that moves with the storm.

plausibility.summary: F7 abrasive winds and F5 dense air impose high shear on exposed profiles; F15 already selects silica–sulfur composites with expansion joints. Laminated plates that ratchet and slide distribute thermomechanical stress like segmented armor, which is mechanically honest at 150–450°C where bulk silica would crack. Silicon biochemistry here remains highly speculative (Bains 2004; Petkowski, Bains & Seager 2020): siloxane backbones need low H₂O and anoxia (F10–F11), so carapace is mineralized tissue, not arbitrary fantasy metal.

journal.en: They walk sideways not for evasion, but to harvest the world's vibration; the universe is their battery.

plausibility.summary: Reframe Crystal Stride: piezo joints provide footing feedback, joint locking, and minor charge for neural control; stamina bonus is efficiency on brittle terrain, not battery-like locomotion. Keep sideways-only as biomechanical specialization, not primary energy harvest.

chains.trait: Asymmetric crushing claws for prying supercritical vent seals.
links: Pries supercritical CO₂/SO₂ vents to access chemosynthetic redox gradients
Dense crust requires mechanical advantage to access reduced volatiles
Reduced volatiles are locked in high-pressure mineral traps requiring leverage

skill.effect: Pries open geological vents, releasing gas clouds for loot and exposing hidden mineral crusts; deals high damage to rock.

chains.weakness: Claws can jam if silica cements them in place; vulnerable if locked in rock by player or rival.
observe: Cracks basalt to release sulfurous plumes and heat
One claw is a hammer, the other a chisel, working in opposition
Feeds on the mineral crust that rapidly reforms around the pry point

journal.en: Geology is their garden; they crack the rock to harvest the breath, prying life from the planet's fever dream.

plausibility.summary: F9 reduced H₂S, FeS₂, and supercritical CO₂ pockets at vents supply the diet and loot loop; mechanical leverage to breach mineral seals is convergent with vent-mining niches. Hammer–chisel asymmetry is workable under F15 mineralized claws; jamming via silica cement fits F7 dust deposition on wet mineral crusts. Eating reforming sulfide crust post-pry aligns with F13 anoxic sulfur redox and FeS₂ grinding niche. Player 'high damage to rock' is gameplay exaggeration but behavior root is honest.

body_plan.origin: Converged from a radially laminated silicate stack lineage that flattened for wind resistance and developed bilateral girders for lateral stress distribution.

temperament: Guarded, territorial of heat patches, defensive against wind shear.
secrets: Harvesting a 'Piezo-Core' from a dead Laja-Tres grants the player temporary vibration sensing, allowing detection of hidden vents and seismic predators.
Laja-Tres migrate in perfect synchrony to their thermal stasis dormancy; interrupting the cycle with rapid cooling causes a mass freeze event, stunning the herd but making them vulnerable.
moments: The heat haze shimmers, and a ridge of rock seems to slide sideways before your eyes, only to freeze into stillness as you approach, indistinguishable from the stone until the shadow of your ship passes and it resumes its slow, grinding march.

journal.en: Three slabs of basalt with legs. Or maybe legs grew slabs. Hard to tell when the wind howls.

Carcinisation? Please. The universe didn't fall in love with crabs; it just learned that flat, brittle things survive high pressure and brittle joints. A different lineage, same low-drag solution. Nature is a lazy engineer; it keeps finding the same angle.
